titleText.es: Hay por ahí una empresa que realmente ha descubierto una forma de alargar los penes, pero es incapaz de alcanzar clientes potenciales.
titleText.en: Somewhere out there is a company that has actually figured out how to enlarge penises, and it's helpless to reach potential customers.
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish archive closely translates the official title text. Both connect the strip's fake web prize to implausible advertising claims; this wording is not printed inside the comic.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: got; picked up (a car or other item)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Pillado is the completed-action form of pillar. In informal Spain Spanish, pillar can mean to get, obtain, or pick up something; with has, it asks about an action connected to the present.

example.es: He pillado un coche de segunda mano.
example.en: I have picked up a second-hand car.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; begins de lo más before a description
cardDefinitions.noteEn: De is the first fixed piece of de lo más, an expression that raises the degree of the description that follows.

example.es: La visita fue de lo más agradable.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; middle piece of de lo más
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Lo is neutral here: it does not stand for a masculine object. Learn it as part of the fixed degree expression de lo más.

example.es: La visita fue de lo más agradable.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Inside de lo más, más strengthens the following description. The whole expression is usually translated together rather than word by word.

example.es: El resultado es de lo más extraño.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Curioso can describe something as strange or noteworthy, not only a person who wants to know more.
Compramos has the same spelling for present ‘we buy’ and completed-past ‘we bought.’ Time words and the surrounding story show which reading is intended.
Premio can name something won or awarded, including a promotional prize.
Visitante has the same singular form for a male or female visitor: el visitante or la visitante.
Quisieron is a completed-past form of querer for ellos, ellas, or ustedes. In a negative sentence, no quisieron can mean that they did not want something or refused it.

example.en: They did not want the prize.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Vieron is the completed-past form of ver for ellos, ellas, or ustedes.
An anuncio can be a notice that informs readers or an advertisement that promotes something.

example.es: Vi el anuncio en la página web.
example.en: I saw the notice on the website.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: but; after all (introduces an emphatic objection or reminder)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: This is standard unaccented si at the start of an exclamation: it pushes back or reminds someone of an obvious fact. It is not accented sí, ‘yes,’ and it does not set a condition as in si llueve, ‘if it rains.’

cardDefinitions.answerEn: was; forms an ongoing past action with an -ando or -iendo form
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Estaba is a past form of estar for I, he, she, or one thing. Before an ongoing-action form such as parpadeando, it presents an action in progress in the past.
Parpadeando is the ongoing-action form of parpadear. It can describe eyes blinking or a light repeatedly switching on and off.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How can you strongly raise the degree of a description, meaning ‘very’ or ‘extremely’?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use the fixed words de lo más, then the describing word.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The plus sign means ‘followed by.’ De lo más stays fixed and is translated as a unit. The following describing word can change in its ordinary way to match what it describes: curioso, curiosa, curiosos, curiosas.

example.es: Las historias son de lo más curiosas.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that something apparently is a certain way, or answer ‘apparently’ by itself?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use parece ser before the description; parece ser can also stand alone when the missing information is already clear.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Parece changes for time if needed, while ser stays in its unchanged dictionary form: parecía ser means ‘it seemed to be.’ A following noun or description can state what seems true.

example.en: It seems to be a good option.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you add ‘and all that’ or ‘and everything like that’ after one detail?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use the fixed conversational expression y todo eso.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The expression loosely adds other similar details without listing them. Eso points back to the kind of thing just mentioned; it does not identify one new object.

example.es: Trajo luces, música y todo eso.
example.en: He brought lights, music, and all that.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: premio al visitante número 100.000.000 · anuncio parpadeante en la web
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Early web advertisements often falsely claimed that the viewer was a numbered visitor who had won a valuable prize. Flashing text was meant to attract clicks, not prove that a real prize existed.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The speakers treat the familiar fake promotion literally: they bought a car for the supposed winner and assume the winner simply missed the flashing notice. The official title text extends the joke to other implausible advertising claims that legitimate businesses would struggle to distinguish from spam.

applications.explanationEn: De lo más is the fixed degree expression, and curioso supplies the description being strengthened.
Lo replaces the masculine singular car and appears immediately before the conjugated verb compramos.
Compramos presents buying the car as one completed event in the story.
Nuestra takes the feminine singular form because the owned noun web is feminine singular here.
